meta.title: Session N4 decision analysis - sell before expiry vs renew/extend (Central LA Jack in the Box NNN)
meta.unit: terminal wealth at 2040 per $1.00 of current annual NOI (illustrative-assumption model; see model_output.json)
meta.privacy: No owner-private value is used. Contract rent, expiry, option terms, basis and debt remain blank (N90, N91).

options.name: SELL_NOW_1031
options.label: Sell now and reinvest through a Section 1031 like-kind exchange
options.how: List now; close before any expiry deterioration; identify replacement net-lease assets with the intermediary; defer gain (S18).
pros: Leaves the parcel before the WALT cliff
Converts an assumed cap rate into cash at today's market
Best modelled downside (highest P05, lowest volatility)
cons: Pays transfer taxes now (0.11% county; 4.56%-6.06% if in-city with ULA - S05/S06)
Forfeits future rent growth if the market re-rates favourably
Requires replacement pipeline (Q11) and tax advice (Q12)
options.conditions: Best when the appraised going-in cap is at or above the solved breakeven (7.81% exit-cap breakeven at n=7 implies selling is rational if your achievable reinvestment yield exceeds ~8.64%, or if the exit-cap outlook is adverse).

options.name: HOLD_TO_EXPIRY
options.label: Hold to the 2030-2035 expiry and sell at expiry
options.how: Do nothing structural; sell in the expiry window.
pros: Collects full contractual rent while it runs
Wins when exit caps stay at or below ~7.8% (n=7 case)
cons: Tenant contraction risk runs the whole period (R01/R02)
Vacancy-at-expiry branch is the single worst outcome across prior workbooks
options.conditions: Only rational with (a) appraised cap clearly below breakeven AND (b) strong confidence in renewal at or above in-place rent AND (c) insurance/ hazard facts confirmed.

options.name: EXTEND_THEN_SELL
options.label: Negotiate an extension / blend-and-extend now, then sell into the longer term
options.how: Open a confidential extension inquiry: term for a fair-market rent reset with CPI-linked escalators; keep a 1031 exit prepared in parallel; sell once term is bankable.
pros: Highest modelled mean and highest best-share (56.6%)
Term is the asset: buyers pay for WALT (thesis must be evidenced - Q06)
Turns an unknown expiry into a priced, longer cash flow
cons: Depends on a contracting tenant agreeing to terms (R11)
If the tenant refuses, time is lost unless the sale track stayed warm
options.conditions: Best when the tenant will sign at or above in-place rent with acceptable guaranty; uplift assumptions (flat/modest/strong) are illustrative.

options.name: DO_NOTHING
options.label: Defer the decision (no extension, no sale preparation)
pros: None modelled - dominated in every statistic
cons: Lowest mean, lowest P05, never best in 10,000 trials
Guarantees walking into the WALT cliff unprepared
options.conditions: Not recommended in any modelled state.

breakevens.note: All from model_output.json on the terminal-wealth basis with w=6.5%, g=2%, c0=6.5% (assumptions). Re-solve once Q01-Q04 are known.
breakevens.reinvest_yield_identity_note: The reinvest breakeven is identical across expiry years by algebra, not by error: with exit cap equal to going-in cap and identical transfer taxes, the (1-a^n) terms cancel and w* = (1+g)/a - 1 where a = (1-transfer)/(c0 + 1 - transfer). Independently re-derived and matched to six decimals.
breakevens.reading: If you can reinvest sale proceeds above 8.64% (assumption basis), selling now wins in every expiry year; if your exit cap would exceed the exit-cap breakeven for the realistic year, holding to that year loses. Both thresholds are assumption-dependent until the real rent, expiry and appraisal arrive.

triggers.when: Appraisal / broker opinion shows going-in cap at or above the solved breakeven for the realistic expiry year
Appraisal shows going-in cap clearly below breakeven AND tenant signs extension at or above in-place rent
triggers.action: Execute OPT-C (extend, then sell into the term).

triggers.when: Tenant refuses any acceptable extension by a time-boxed date (suggested: 2027-06-30)
triggers.action: Fall back to OPT-A and sell in 2027-2028 with whatever term remains, through 1031.

triggers.when: Parcel turns out to be inside City of Los Angeles limits
triggers.action: Add 0.45% base + 4.0%/5.5% ULA to every exit scenario before listing; confirm threshold in force at closing (S05, S06).

triggers.when: Insurance quote exceeds an amount the owner finds unacceptable (owner sets the number - Q08)
triggers.action: Bias to OPT-A; an unpriceable insurance line invalidates long holds.

triggers.when: Less than ~6 years of term remain and no extension is signed
triggers.action: Do not hold passively: sell or extend immediately (financing cliff).

triggers.when: Tenant credit deteriorates further (system SSS below -2%, accelerated closures, lease-rejection language in 10-Q)
triggers.action: Accelerate OPT-A; do not extend term on a weakening covenant without credit support.

triggers.when: Replacement pipeline for 1031 is not viable within the statutory windows
triggers.action: Re-run OPT-A as a taxable sale only after Q12 (tax rates) is answered; do not close 1031 blind.

recommended_course_of_action.decision: DUAL TRACK, time-boxed: (1) open a confidential extension / blend-and-extend inquiry now targeting >=10 years of term at or above in-place rent with CPI-linked escalators and a strengthened guaranty; (2) in parallel, prepare a Section 1031 sale so the asset can be sold quickly if the extension fails or the appraisal clears the breakeven; (3) never let the asset drift into the final 3-4 years of term unmanaged.
recommended_course_of_action.why: OPT-C has the highest modelled expectation (mean 41.46, best in 56.6% of trials); OPT-A has the best modelled tail (P05 27.98, sd 6.80) and is the hedge against tenant refusal and exit-cap risk; OPT-B and OPT-D are dominated or near-dominated. The dual track keeps both live, which is exactly what the fifteen prior workbooks independently converged on (see reconciliation.json).
recommended_course_of_action.confidence: Moderate on the shape of the decision (sequence), low on any specific number until the owner facts (Q01-Q04) and parcel facts (Q05, Q08, Q09) arrive. All model outputs are assumption-driven (IR-14).
recommended_course_of_action.wealth_preservation_balance: Risk is managed by: time-boxing (T3, T6), keeping the sale option warm (dual track), confirming insurance/hazards before any long hold (T5), and diversifying a concentrated single-asset position through the 1031 branch (R17).
